title: Find the Count of Monotonic Pairs I
summary: Given an array of positive integers nums of length n, find the number of pairs of non-negative integer arrays (arr1, arr2) such that arr1 is monotonically non-decreasing, arr2 is monotonically non-increasing, and arr1[i] + arr2[i] equals nums[i] for all indices i.
statement: Given an array of positive integers nums of length n, find the number of pairs of non-negative integer arrays (arr1, arr2) such that arr1 is monotonically non-decreasing, arr2 is monotonically non-increasing, and arr1[i] + arr2[i] equals nums[i] for all indices i. The result should be returned modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Count nonnegative arrays arr1 and arr2 with arr1 nondecreasing, arr2 nonincreasing, and arr1[i]+arr2[i]=nums[i].
hints: Choosing arr1 fixes arr2, so each transition only needs bounds on the previous arr1 value.
DP by index and current arr1 value; valid predecessors end at min(current, current+previous_num-current_num).
Use prefix sums of the previous DP row to total all valid predecessors in O(1).
The bound simultaneously expresses arr1 nondecreasing and arr2 nonincreasing, so every valid pair is counted once.
editorial: The bound simultaneously expresses arr1 nondecreasing and arr2 nonincreasing, so every valid pair is counted once.

tests.explanation: Exactly four compatible choices of the nondecreasing first array determine valid second arrays.
The number of nondecreasing four-term choices from zero through five is 126.
